caseno: First Appeal No. 68 of 2002 with C. Rule No. 282 (F) of 2002.
lawyer:
Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed with SM Monir, Advocates------- For the Appellant. 
Hasan Foez, Siddique with M Habibullah, Advocates------- for respondent Nos. 1 to 8. 
Abdun Nur with Imam Hossain------- For Respondent No. 19.
parties:
NFM Universeum Estate Ltd ------ Appellant
Vs.
ANM Obaidul Islam and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rashid J: Defendant No. 14 presented the appeal against the decree dated 22-11-01 passed by the Fifth Court of Joint District Judge at Dhaka in Title Suit No. 135 of 1997, which decreed the suit.

2. One ANM Obaidul Islam, predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos. 1 to 8 as plaintiff instituted title Suit No. 120 of 1992 for declaration of title and recovery of possession of the suit land measuring about 51 decimals, which was fully described in the schedule to the plaint. The suit was then renumbered as aforesaid title Suit No. 137 of 1997.

3. Plaint case, in short, is that the suit land along with other land of CS Plot No. 158 originally belonged to one Abdul Kader and the record of rights were finally prepared and published in his name in CS khatian No. 4. Then, by a, registered deed of sale Abdul Kader transferred the entire land of said CS plot to Sharat Chandra Ghosh, Advocate. Sharat Chandra Ghosh possessed the land through 'Bargaders' Sheik Asanullah alias Munshi and Sheikh Mohammad for some time.Sharat Chandra Ghosh left a will giving the entire land of said plot to Premtosh Chandra Gosh and Bimal Chandra Chosh by a registered will dated 24 Ashar 1335 BS. The will was then duly probated on 13-7-35 in Probate Case No. 7 of 1934.

4. By a registered deed of sale dated 24-9-46 Premtosh Chandra Gosh and Bimal Chandra Ghosh transferred 70 decimals of said CS plot No. 158 to Sheikh Hasenuddin and delivered possession to him Sheik Hasenuddin thus possessed said 70 decimals of land and died leaving Samiruddin and others. Samiruddin and seven others sold said 70 decimals of land by two registered sale deeds dated 12-9-55 to aforesaid ANM Obaidul Islam and his wife Mostammat Rowshanara Begum alias Gulshan Begum transferring to each of them 35 decimals and delivered possession.

5. During survey under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, 66 decimals instead of 70 decimals was equally recorded in their names in SA khatian Nos. 197 and 196 respectively. At the time of RS survey, 33 decimals was similarly recorded in the name of each of them in RS khatian Nos. 202 and 225 respectively.

6. Obaidul Islam instituted Title Suit No. 303 of 1990 for a declaration that he purchased 35 decimals of land in the 'Benami' of his wife Gulshan Begum and on 6-8-92 got a compromise decree to that effect that Gulshan Begum was his 'Benamder'. Out of the suit land, 15 decimals were acquired in LA Case Nos. 40A and 40B of 1989-90 and they got the compensation as per award. Obaidul Islam made a waqf of 35 decimals of land and on 4-6-88 and 27-8-89 made applications for supplementary list with the Engineer Obaidul Islam Waqf Estate being EC No. 16392. While Obaidul Islam was thus in exclusive possession of the suit land, on 9-1-92 defendant Nos. 1 to 8 dispossessed him therefrom. Hence, the suit.

7. During the proceeding of the suit, on 10-4-96 Obaidul Islam died leaving the present plaintiffs as his only legal representatives.

8. Defendant No. 14 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the plaint case. Its case, in short, is that the suit land along with other land belonged to Abdul Kader and CS record of rights was finally prepared and published in his name. Abdul Kader bequeathed the entire land of CS plot No. 158 by a registered deed of gift being 4133 dated 31-5-1917 to his three sons Sheikh Elahi Bux, Sheikh Abdul Karim and Sheikh Abdul Nabi and put them into possession. On 16-4-43 by way of family settlement Sheikh Elahi Bux and Sheikh Karim got the suit plot in their shares. Successive heirs of Sheik Elahi Bux and Sheik Abdul Karim, namely, Aziza Begum, Serajul Islam, Tehera Begum, Sonaban Bibi, Abdul Motaleb, Abdus Shahid and Abdul Hamid, jointly possessed the suit land along with other land by cultivation and growing fruits openly, publicly and adversely to the entire world.

9. Then, by a registered deed of sale dated 4-7-95 all those successors of Elahi Bux and Abdul Karim transferred 49.5 decimals out of said CS plot No. 158 to said defendant No. 14 and delivered possession. Defendant No. 14 had since then been possessing said 49.50 decimals of land. It got its name mutated in respect of said land and had been paying rent. It filled the land with earth and erected boundary walls surrounding said land and also made semi-pucca structures thereon. It got water, gas and electricity connection to the land.

10. Defendant No. 11 RAJUK also filed a written statement denying the case of the plaintiff. It although cross-examined the witness of the plaintiff but did not adduce any evidence. It contended that the suit was not maintainable without prior notice under section 169 of Town Improvement Act, 1953.

11. On the party pleadings the following issues were finally settled:

(a) Was the suit maintainable in the manner and form as framed?

(b) Was the suit barred by limitation?

(c) Had the plaintiff got title and possession in the suit land?

(d) Was the plaintiff entitled to get a decree as prayed for? and

(e) What relief the plaintiff was entitled to.

12. In support of their case, the plaintiffs examined three witnesses and adduced number of documents, which were marked as Exhibits 1 to 20. Defendant No. 14 also examined three witnesses and its documents were marked as Exhibits 'Ka' to 'cha'.

13. PW 1 Md Ruhul Amin testified that he was plaintiff No. 3 and deposing on behalf of all plaintiffs. He deposed in support of the plaint case and tendered the documents into evidence.

14. He stated that the suit land was a part of CS plot No. 158 appertaining to CS khatian No.4. The plot comprised of 5.68 acres. The suit land was finally recorded and published in the name of Abdul Kader. By a deed being No. 351 dated 12-1-1921, Exhibit 1, Abdul Kader transferred the entire land of said CS plot No. 158 to one Sharat Chandra Ghosh, Advocate, Sharat Chandra Ghosh possessed the suit land through 'Bargaders' Sheik Ahsanullah Munshi and Sheikh Mohammad who gave a joint registered 'Barga kabuliyat' being deed No. 2810 dated 19-5-1924, Exhibit 2(ka) for a period of six years. Then, Sharat Chandra Ghosh left a will executed by him on 24 Ashar 1335 BS giving the entire land of said CS plot No. 158 to Premtosh Chandra Ghosh and Bimal Chandra Ghosh. After death of Sharat Chandra Ghosh, they on 19-7-1935 obtained a probate of the will in Probate Case NO.7 of 1934, Exhibits 3 and 6.

15. By a registered deed of sale being No. 4030 dated 24-9-1946 said Premtosh Chandra Ghosh and Bimal Chandra Ghosh transferred 70 decimals of land to Sheikh Hasenuddin. The original deed of Sheik Hasenuddin was adduced and marked Exhibit 4. After the death of Sheikh Hasenuddin, his heirs Samiruddin and others by two deeds being No. 6266 and 6268 dated 12-9-1955 transferred 70 decimals of land to Obaidul Islam and his wife Gulshan Begum and delivered possession. Original deeds were adduced and marked Exhibits 5 and 5(ka). During survey under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the suit land was recorded equally in SA khatian Nos. 196 and 197 in the name of his father and mother, Exhibit 7 and 7(ka). Similarly, RS khatian Nos. 202 and 225, 7(kha) and 7(ga) were also prepared in the names of his parents. In the RS khatian a road was shown wrongly. Consequently, his father filed two written objections, which were accepted and mistake was corrected vide Exhibits 9 series.

16. He stated that in the suit land, paddy was cultivated by his father and a pond was made by cutting earth. His father let out some huts on the land to different tenants and received rents, Exhibit 10 series. He stated that when the Public Health Engineering Department tried to take a sewerage line over the land his father raised objections: He made applications before different authorities including the Chief Martial Law Administrator. Consequently, construction of sewerage line stopped, Exhibit 11 to 11 (chha). In 1988, his father made waqf of 35 decimals of land and addressed two applications to the Waqf Administrator for supplementary list of the Engineer Obaidul Islam Waqf Estate, being EC No. 16392. After death of his father, the Waqf Administrator however, rejected the applications by his order dated 7-7-97, Exhibit 12.

17. He also stated that his father purchased half of the suit land in the name 'Benami' of his mother. He then instituted Title Suit No. 303 of 1990 in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge for declaration that his mother was 'Benamder' of his father. The suit ended in a compromise decree declaring his mother was 'Benamder' of his father. The plaint, decree and 'Solenama' were adduced and marked Exhibits 13, 13(ka) and 13(kha). Some portion of the suit land measuring 15 decimals was acquired in LA Case No. 40A of 1989-90 and 40B of 1989-90. Award was given in the names of plaintiffs. They withdrew the money. Notices for acquisition and information slips about payment of compensation were marked Exhibits 14, 14(ka), l4(kha) and 14(ga).

18. He stated that defendant Nos. 1 to 8 instituted Title Suit No. 17 of 1993 for perpetual injunction restraining the defendants from receiving the compensation for acquisition. The suit was dismissed on 8-9-93. Appeal therefrom being Title Appeal No. 318 of 1993 was also dismissed on 29-4-95; judgments and decrees were adduced and marked Exhibit 15 series.

19. He stated that said defendants instituted Title Suit No. 296 of 1989, which was renumbered as Title Suit No. 47 of 1990 and got an ex parte decree. Against the ex parte decree, miscellaneous case being No. 12 of 1994, No. 13 of 1994 and No. 14 of 1994 were filed under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex parte decree. Ultimately, all the miscellaneous cases were allowed and ex parte decree was set aside by judgment and order dated 28-4-97, Exhibit 17. The plaintiffs also instituted Title Suit No. 221 of 1995, which was renumbered as Title Suit No. 134 of 1997 but ultimately, withdrew the suit after the ex parte decree dated 19-11-90 was set aside, Exhibit 17(chha).

20. Meanwhile, on the basis of said ex parte decree, said defendant Nos. 1 to 8 on 9-1-92 dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land by forcibly entering into the suit land therein and breaking the huts. The defendants then erected furniture shop in the suit land in order to change the nature and character of the suit land.

21. In cross-examination, he stated that total suit land was 66 decimals. Entire land of the suit plot was 5.68 acres. He could not say what was the adjacent east plot of CS plot No. 158 and who possessed. Similarly, he said that he had no knowledge who was on the adjacent west of CS plot No. 158 and what was plot number. He denied that he did not know CS plot No. 158. He stated that he did not know plot No. 158 right on the spot. He was aged 49 years old. He did not see the 'Bargaders'. He did not bring any witness to prove 'Borga'. He did not file the rent receipts of Sheikh Hasenuddin. He did not see him personally possessing the suit land. The Waqf Administrator informed that the suit land was not included in the existing waqf. He was not aware whether there was any partition amongst the owners of plot No. 158. He did not make parties all the owners of the plot.

22. To cross-examination by defendant No. II, he stated that he did not give notice before the suit to the RAJUK but subsequently issued summons.

23. On recall, he stated that to the east of the suit land was Rafiqul Kader Chowdhury and others, to the west 29 Uttar Dhanmondi, Kalabagan (land of Masuda), to the north, road of Panthapath and south 41 and 30 north Dhanmondi, Kalabagan.

24. PW 2 Md Ali Akbar, aged about 90 years. He testified that he knew Obaidul Islam and worked with him. They were lecturers in the Engineering College. He knew the suit land, which was near his house. In 1955, they purchased land of so it plot together. Plaintiff purchased the suit land and got possession. He knew children of Obaidul Islam. They were dispossessed 8/9 years ago. Before dispossession, the plaintiff possessed the suit land. At the time defendant No. 14 possessed but he did not know him. He had no title.

25. In cross-examination, he reiterated that in 1955 they got possession. At the time, there was paddy field. He denied that he did not see the suit land. Defendant No. 14 possessed for 8/9 years. At the time, there were small huts on the suit land. There were tenants of Obaidul Islam on his land. Now they were not there. He did not know the defendants. He again stated that the defendant possessed the suit land for last 8/9 years.

26. PW 3 Monirul Alam Chowdhury, aged about 57 years, testified that he was working as Professor in Kalyanpur Mohila College. He knew Obaidul Islam and also the suit land. He also knew the children of Obaidul Islam. Obaidul Islam became owner by purchase and since then possessed. He also erected huts. In 1992, Obaidul Islam was dispossessed from the suit land. He did not know them who dispossessed him.

27. In cross-examination, he stated that Obaidul Islam was his brother-in-law. He denied that he was deposing for the interest of his nephews and nieces. He could not say who dispossessed the plaintiff in 1992.

28. SyedMd Delawar Hossain was examined as Advocate Commissioner. He deposed that he was the member of Dhaka Bar and appointed an Advocate Commissioner. After holding investigation he submitted his report dated 12-5-98.

29. Abdul Awal Minto on behalf of defendant No. 14 was examined as DW 1 on commission. He deposed in support of its written statement. He admitted that the entire land of plot No. 158 belonged to Abdul Kader and CS record of rights was prepared in his name. He claimed that by a registered deed of gift dated 31-5-17, Exhibit "kha" Abdul Kader transferred the entire land of CS plot No. 158 to his three sons, namely, Elahi Bux, Abdul Karim and Abdul Nabi and delivered possession. In 1943, by way of family settlement Sheikh Abdul Karim and Sheikh Elahi Bux got the suit land in their share. Elahi Bux then died leaving behind two sons Sayeed Hossain and Siddique Hossain, Sheikh Abdul Karim also died leaving one son Miah Hossain, Sayeed Hossain died leaving one son Arju Mia, Siddique Hossain died leaving one wife Aziza, one daughter Tahera Begum and one son Sirajul Islam, Arzu died leaving one wife Tahera Khatun. Miah Hossain died leaving one wife Sonaban Bibi, three sons Abdul Motaleb, Abdul Shahid and Abdul Hamid. The successive heirs of Elahi Bux and Abdul Karim used to possess the suit land by cultivation. SA record of rights was prepared in the names of various persons but not recorded in the names of Sonaban and others as they were illiterate. Accordingly, they instituted Title Suit No. 47 of 1990, which was decreed on 28-11-90. By a deed being No. 2725 dated 4-7-75 Exhibit "ga" he purchased 49.5 decimals of land from Sonaban Bibi and others and got possession. He got his name mutated, Exhibit  gha He filled the suit land with earth and got a boundary wall erected around the suit land. Nobody obstructed them. His people was living there. He got the connection of gas, electricity and water, etc. to the suit land Exhibit "uma" . He got a municipality holding number which is 4412/a, North Dhanmondi Exhibit "cha" series. The plaintiffs and their predecessor had no title and possession in the suit land. He denied that on 12-1-21 Abdul Kader transferred the suit land to Sharat Chandra Ghosh or he possessed ever.

30. In cross-examination, he testified that he was doing business. On 6-4-99 he submitted written statement. He could not say as to whether the papers were submitted along with his written statement. Whether or not on 21-3-01 he submitted the papers, he could not say, his Advocate could say. He could not say whether the deed No. 4133, Exhibit "kha'' was submitted in Title Suit No. 47 of 1990. The seal on the deed reads Mymensingh. He denied that the date 31-5-1917 on the deed was written recently. One page stamp was valued one Taka two Annas and subsequent two papers were cartridges. He denied that those cartridges were Bangladeshi. He denied that there was no entry in the ledger book of the Sub-registry and that cartridge papers were not of the British time, having no mark of lion. He also denied that the deed was of recent writing and created recently. He did not know any of the witnesses to the deed and he was not born then. To the question of the commission as to whether he claimed the land of RS plot Nos. 1207, 1208 and 1209, he answered he could say only by looking through the papers and record. He did not know whether said plots were recorded in the name of the plaintiff. He denied that the suit land was recorded in plot Nos. 1207, 1208 and 1209.

31. DW 2 Md Abdur Rashed, aged about 48 years. He deposed that he knew the defendant but did not know the suit land. The defendant No. 14 possessed the suit land since 1995. Before him Sonaban Bibi and others were in possession. Since 1979-80 he saw them. At the time it was pond, bamboo clumps and paddy field. He never saw the plaintiff possessed any part of the suit land.

32. In cross-examination, he stated that he was doing business. He witnessed the deed of the defendant who purchased from Sonaban Bibi and others. Entire land of CS plot No. 158 was 13.5 acres. He did not receive any summons.

33. DW 3 Md Riazuddin Akand, aged about 50 years, deposed that he knew the defendant and also the suit land. Defendant No. 14 possessed the suit land since 1995. Before him Sonaban and others possessed. They possessed since 1980. There was ditch earlier now that was filled with earth. He did not see the plaintiff before the defendant.

34. In cross-examination, he stated that he was a teacher of Tejgaon Polytechnic Government College. Defendant No. 14 possessed western part of the suit plot. He could not say the quantity of the land in suit. 	.

35. These are all the evidence adduced by the parties.

36. Upon the aforesaid evidence, oral and documentary, learned Joint District Judge decreed the suit on contest against contesting defendants and ex parte against the rest declaring title of the plaintiffs in the suit land and directed the concerned defendant to hand over vacant possession to the plaintiff within sixty days from date.

37. Only issue facing us is, whether the learned Joint District Judge was justified in decreeing the suit.

38. As stated above, admittedly CS plot No. 158 appertaining to CS khatian No.4 including the suit land originally belonged to Abdul Kader and CS record of rights was finally prepared and published in his name.

39. It is the case of the plaintiff that Abdul Kader transferred the entire land of CS plot No. 158 to Sharat Chandra Ghosh, Advocate by a registered deed of sale being No. 351 dated 12-1-1921 and delivered possession. A certified copy of said document was adduced by the plaintiffs and marked Exhibit 2. Sharat Chandra Ghosh possessed the suit land for some time through 'Bargaders'. namely, Sheik Asanullah Munshi and Sheik Mohammad by executing registered 'Barga Kabuliyat' dated 19-5-1924. The plaintiffs adduced a certified copy of the Kabuliyat which was marked Exhibit 2(kha). Sharat Chandra Ghosh gave the suit land to Premtosh Ghosh and Bimal Chandra Ghosh by a registered deed of will executed on 24 Ashar 1335 BS. The will was duly proved on 13-11-1934 and probate granted thereon on 19-7-35 in Probate Case No.7 of 1934. To prove the will and probate, the plaintiffs adduced a certified copy of the will, Exhibit 6 and suit register of said Probate Case No. 7 of 1934, Exhibit 3. In the column, "order made and date" of the suit register, it was recorded that the will was proved on 13-11-1934 and probated on 13-7-1935. Premtosh Chandra Ghosh and Bimal Chandra then transferred 70 decimals of CS plot No. 158 to Hasenuddin by a registered deed of sale dated 24-9- 46. The plaintiff adduced the original deed, which was marked Exhibit 1. After death of Hasenuddin, his heirs Samiruddin and seven others by two registered deeds of sale dated 12-9-1955 transferred equally said 70' decimals of land to Obaidul Islam, original plaintiff and his wife Gulshan Begum. Those deeds were adduced and marked as Exhibit 5 and 5(ka). During survey under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 66 decimals instead of 70 decimals was equally recorded in the names of Obaidul. Islam and his wife Gulshan Begum in SA khatian Nos. 196 and 197 Exhibit 7 and 7(ka). During RS survey said land was again recorded as RS plot Nos. 1207, 1208 and 1209 in RS khatian Nos. 202 and 225 in their names Exhibit 7(kha) and 7(ga). The plaintiffs adduced rent receipts showing payment of rents, Exhibit 8 series and counterfoils evidencing possession through tenants, Exhibit 10 series.

40. Obaidul Islam made a waqf of 35 decimals of land. But his prayer for supplementary list with the Engineer Obaidul Islam Waqf Estate was rejected by the Waqf Administration by his order dated 7-7-97 Exhibit 12.

41. Out of 66 decimals, 15 decimals were acquired in LA Case Nos. 40A and 40B of 1989-90. The plaintiffs adduced the notices for acquisition and also the information slips showing payment of the compensation to the plaintiffs, Exhibits 14, 14(ka), 14(kha) and 14(ga).

42. Meanwhile Obaidul Islam instituted Title Suit No. 303 of 1990 for a declaration that he purchased 35 decimals of land in the 'Benami' of his wife Gulshan Begum from Samiruddin and others. The suit ended in compromise and Gulshan Begum was declared to be 'Benami' of Obaidul Islam. Plaintiff adduced the plaint, compromise petition and decree of the suit vide Exhibit 13 series. Public Health Engineering Department once wanted to take sewerage line through the land of the plaintiffs. Obaidul Islam raised objections thereto. He even wrote to Chief Martial Law Administrator. The project was ultimately abandoned. In support, the plaintiffs produced the letters written by Obaidul Islam to different authorities, Exhibit 11 series.

43. PW 2 Md Ali Akbar aged about 90 years corroborated PW 1 that he along with Obaidul Islam purchased land out of said CS plot No. 158 together and became owners and in 1955 they got possession. He and Obaidul possessed their land. Then Obaidul Islam was dispossessed from the land 8/9 years ago. PW 3 also corroborated PW 1 on possession. They appear to be respected people. We could not find any reason for them for not telling the truth on oath.

44. Mr Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Senior Advocate, submitted that the evidence of the plaintiffs on title and possession were insufficient. The magnitude of above voluminous documentary evidence along with oral evidence adduced by the plaintiffs in support of their title and possession is so great that we cannot appreciate such submission.

45. He particularly stressed that Exhibits 2, 2(ka), 3 and 6 were certified copies and the plaintiffs did not prove them by calling for the orizinal volume from the office of Sub-Registrar. As such, the documents do not prove title of the plaintiffs.

46. In reply, Mr Hasan Foez Siddique, learned Advocate for the respondents, drew our attention to the judgment dated 8-9-93 passed in Title Suit No. 17 of 1993 brought by defendant Nos. 1 to 8, Exhibit 15(kha). In the suit, very same certified copy was adduced by the plaintiffs and marked as Exhibit B. DW 7 Khandker Mosharraf Hossain, record keeper, brought the volume and proved the certified copy as correct tallying with the entries made in the volume. In the judgment dated 29-4-95 passed in Title Appeal No. 318 of 1993, said deed dated 11-1-1921, Exhibit B was considered and the appellate Court found that the plaintiffs. i.e. defendant Nos. 1 to 8 there, failed to prove that the deed was created. Besides, Exhibit 3 certified copy of suit register, which clearly recorded that on 19-7-1935 the will of Sharat Chandra Ghosh was probated in Probate Case No.7 of 1934. In view of the above, we do not think the plaintiffs were required to prove the certified copy again by calling for the volume from the office of the Sub-registrar.

47. Mr Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed submitted that the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession before dispossession. He also referred to the deposition of the plaintiffs' witnesses. Defendant Nos. 1 to 8 who dispossessed the plaintiffs did not contest the suit. So, practically the evidence of the plaintiffs on possession followed by dispossession got a walkover. As defendant No. 14 purchased the suit land in 1995 from said defendant Nos. 1 to 8 and possessed since then, had got no locus standi to contest the case of possession and dispossession of the plaintiffs.

48. Mr Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed also submitted that the present suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession without a prayer for partition of CS plot No. 158 was not maintainable as number of people now owned and possessed the land of said plot comprising of about 5.68 acres and no effective decree for title and possession could be passed without the presence of those owners.

49. We find that the suit land was already recorded in the names of original plaintiff Obaidul Islam and his wife Gulshan Begum during survey under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in plot Nos. 298/302 and 298/303 appertaining to SA khatian Nos. 196 and 197. Such record of rights was published some time in 1964. On the basis of such record of rights the plaintiff possessed the suit land exclusively on payment of rents on proper receipt Exhibit 8 series. Similarly, under the RS survey the suit land was again recorded in the names of Obaidul Islam and his wife Gulshan Begum in RS plot Nos. 1207, 1208 and 1209 appertaining to RS khatian Nos. 202 and 225 and RS record of rights was published in 1980s.

<u>50. In view of such exclusive possession of their specific land under distinct and separate holdings for more than 12 years, the plaintiffs no more need partition of their land. Submission of Mr Khandker has therefore got no substance.</u>

51. Lastly, he submitted the suit land out of 5.68 acres was not clearly and properly identified and in the absence of identification, the plaintiffs were not entitled to a decree prayed for.

52. In view of above discussions, we find no substance in the submission of Mr. Khandker. Moreover, defendant Nos. 1 to 8 never contested the identity of the suit property. Nor defendant No. 14 raised any question about the identity of the suit land.

53. In support of its case, defendant No. 14 adduced a deed 4133 dated 31-5-1917 claimed to have been executed and registered by Abdul Kader giving the entire land of CS plot No. 158 measuring 8.44 acres of land to his three sons, Sheikh Elahi Bux, Sheikh Abdul Karim and Sheikh Abdul Nabi. Said defendant tendered the deed into evidence on 24-7-2001 and got it marked Exhibit kha. It is the case of defendant No.14 that after a family settlement Sheikh Elahi Bux and Sheikh Abdul Karim got said land in their share. But no evidence whatsoever was led in support thereof. After their death, their successive heirs Sonaban Bibi and others transferred 49.5 decimals of land to defendant No. 14.

54. Learned Joint District Judge found that the deed was forged and created. He found two cartridges used for the deed of Bangladeshi origin. There was no sign of British time. On being asked, the officer-in-charge of Mymensingh Sadar Sub-Registry could not say that the deed was registered in their office, Exhibit 18. The officer-in-charge further informed that on 14-4-1918 the office of the Sadar Sub-Registry, Mymensingh was burned down by accidental fire. Besides, there was no reason for registration of the deed by Abdul Kader in Mymensingh. We have closely examined the deed. We find the writings on the deed very fresh and of recent origin. So, we do not have any hesitation to affirm the finding of the learned Joint District Judge that said deed Exhibit 'kha' was created by forgery and fabrication for the suit. Mr Khandker however, did not rely upon the deed, in any way.

55. Having full knowledge that the deed was forged, fraudulent and created, DW 1 Abdul Awal Minto on behalf of defendant No. 14 gave the deed into evidence. DW 1 Abdul Awal Minto thereby committed a serious offence making him liable for prosecution under section 195(i)(c) read with section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

56. In the circumstances, ultimate conclusion of the learned Joint District Judge that the plaintiffs successfully proved their title and possession in the suit land and thereupon, he committed no error in decreeing the suit. Such decree does not suffer from any illegality or infirmity. Appeal, therefore, fails.

57. In the result, the appeal is dismissed with cost. Impugned judgment and decree are hereby affirmed and the defendants, particularly defendant No. 14, are directed to vacate the suit land by removing all their structures within a period of thirty days from date.

58. Connected Rule is also discharged with cost. Order of stay granted at the time of issue of the Rule on 19-6-02 staying further proceeding of the execution case is hereby recalled and vacated.

59. In view of above decision, the application of third party for addition does not deserve any consideration and is accordingly, rejected.

60. Let the deed of gift being No. 4133 dated 31-5-1917 Exhibit 'kha' be impounded. The Registrar is directed to immediately take the document in his custody and send the same in safe cover to the Fifth Court of Joint District Judge for prosecution of DW 1 Abdul Awal Minto in accordance with law.

The learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court at Dhaka is hereby directed to make a complaint against DW 1 Abdul Awal Minto under section 195(1)(c) read with section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for using said deed in the suit knowing it to be forged and fraudulent for criminal prosecution.

Send down the records at once.

End.
